Group 1 (Case 1):
Here is the student’s answer for this case:
1. Case 1: Breast apocrine carcinoma
The patient has a left breast mass for over two years with recent enlargement. Ultrasound showing irregular hypoechoic areas and axillary lymph nodes, plus mammographic punctate calcifications, support malignancy. Core needle biopsy demonstrates carcinoma, and immunohistochemistry is positive for GCDFP-15, SOX10, S100, and AR with Ki-67 ~40%, a profile characteristic of apocrine carcinoma. Benign breast neoplasm, cyst, and inflammatory mass are excluded by biopsy and imaging. Invasive lobular carcinoma is unlikely because E-Cadherin is positive, and other special subtypes are less favored due to the strong apocrine markers. The frontier of breast malignancy is therefore refined to breast apocrine carcinoma (invasive carcinoma with apocrine differentiation). Definitive subtyping and staging still require surgical excision pathology.

Here is the reference diagnosis for this case:
1. Case 1: Primary acinic cell carcinoma of the breast
